items.title: PS5 Firmware Update Drops Ahead of GTA 6 as Jailbreak Race Heats Up
points: Sony has released a fresh PS5 firmware update with security fixes, and its timing is raising questions as the console’s jailbreak scene continues to make progress before the GTA 6 launch.
The new system software version 26.07-14.22.00 arrived on November 2, thereby giving the console an opportunity to reinforce its security.
The latest PS5 firmware update is approximately 1.267 GB in size and is available to download now.
What catches the eye of gamers is the security-focused nature of the update and that it arrives right after the recent developments surrounding the PS5 jailbreaks.
This update follows firmware version 14.20 that arrived on October 21.
The homebrew community has been actively exploring the vulnerabilities in Sony’s console and previously released a jailbreak that supports firmware versions 7.00 through 13.60.
Some speculation has emerged that the minimum firmware required to run GTA 6 would be at least version 14.10.
Being such a high-profile game and with GTA 6 launching on PlayStation and Xbox consoles first, this news is really concerning.

items.title: Uttarkashi avalanche: Rescue teams recover tents, bags of 7 missing trekkers, guide
points: Search and rescue teams on Monday found no trace of seven trekkers and a local guide who went missing following an avalanche on the high-altitude Kedartal trek in Uttarakhand’s Uttarkashi district on October 29, officials said on Monday.
The team however recovered tents and bags near Kedar Kharak, the second major campsite at approximately 4,000 metres on the trail, officials said.
The missing trekkers include five men from West Bengal and two women from Uttar Pradesh and a guide from Uttarkashi.
The avalanche struck near Kedar Kharak on October 29 while the group was descending from Kedartal, which is perched at an altitude of 15,485 feet (4,720 metres) in Uttarkashi district.
Beginning from Gangotri, the 18-kilometre trail winds steeply alongside the Kedar Ganga river.
According to officials, the 12-member expedition, comprising seven trekkers and five support staff, set off from Gangotri on October 27 and was scheduled to return on October 29.

items.title: VHP seeks arrest of those who smeared ink on Addanda Cariappa
points: The Legal Cell of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP), South Karnataka, has condemned the alleged attack on former Rangayana Director Addanda Cariappa, whose face was smeared with ink by protesters in Bengaluru on Saturday, and demanded the immediate arrest of…
In a statement issued here on Monday, the VHP described the incident as an “attack on freedom of expression” and said such an act was contrary to the fundamental values of democracy.
It may be recalled that protesters targeted Mr. Cariappa during the staging of a controversial play on Mahatma Gandhi’s assassination in Bengaluru on Saturday.
The protesters had objected to the portrayal of Gandhi in the play.
The VHP has also sought adequate police protection for Mr. Cariappa and a detailed probe to identify those who instigated or encouraged the incident.
Describing the incident as an affront to the dignity and cultural identity of the Kodava community, the VHP demanded appropriate action against those responsible.

items.title: 78-year-old man loses ₹61,000 after mobile phone theft on BMTC bus
points: A 78-year-old man lost ₹61,000 from his bank account after his mobile phone was allegedly stolen while he was travelling on a BMTC bus in Electronic City on October 27.
Layout, Parappana Agrahara, was travelling to Indira Gandhi Hospital in Siddapura with his granddaughter, who was unwell.
According to his complaint, he left home around 9.15 a.m. and boarded a BMTC bus heading towards Majestic at the Hosa Road bus stop around 9.30 a.m.
Shortly after boarding, he noticed that his mobile phone, which he had kept in the upper pocket of his shirt, was missing.
He subsequently proceeded to the hospital, where he left his granddaughter with his daughter, Malashree, and informed her about the theft.
He was shocked to discover that ₹50,000 had been withdrawn through a UPI transaction, followed by another transaction of ₹11,000 on the same day.
She contacted the cybercrime helpline 1930 and advised him to lodge a police complaint.

points: With a little over two weeks for the pilgrimage season at Sabarimala to kick off, the Forest department has stepped up preparations along the traditional trekking route from Erumely, clearing the path and putting basic facilities in place ahead of the…

items.title: Railways intensify security ahead of Deepavali, warn against carrying firecrackers
points: Railway officials warned that carrying firecrackers on trains or onto station premises could pose a serious fire hazard, particularly amid the festive rush, endangering passengers and railway personnel.
Violators will face legal action under the Railways Act, 1989, including imprisonment of up to three years, a fine or both, depending on the applicable provision.
The Railway Protection Force (RPF) has intensified checks using explosive detection equipment and sniffer dogs to prevent the transportation of prohibited and hazardous materials.
CCTV surveillance has also been strengthened, and special teams have been deployed to prevent passenger-related crimes and respond to security concerns.
Additional RPF personnel have been deployed at entry and exit points, platforms and other crowded areas to regulate queues, manage crowds and enhance security.
Major stations, including Chennai Central, Chennai Egmore, Perambur, Tambaram, Chennai Beach, Mambalam and St. Thomas Mount, are under heightened surveillance.

Apart from the five systems contracted in 2018, India's Defence Acquisition Council granted Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) for five more S-400 systems in March this year.

points: Romanian oil and gas producer OMV Petrom is preparing for a leadership change as chief executive Christina Verchere has announced she will not seek another term, with her departure set to occur around the planned startup of the company’s flagship Neptun…
Verchere, who has led the company since May 2018, told supervisory board chair Emma Delaney she will not be available for another mandate after her current term expires on April 16, 2027.

items.title: Mother tongue key to taking science to the masses: KSTA chief
points: Mr. Rajasab stressed the need to make scientific knowledge accessible to the public, particularly through communication in the mother tongue.

He was speaking at the inauguration of the three-day XLIX All India Botanical Conference (AIBC) and the International Symposium on ‘Advances in Plant Sciences and Accelerating Sustainable Innovations for the Bio-economy (APSAIB)’ at CSIR-Central Food…
Emphasising the role of science in nation-building, Mr. Rajasab called for the adoption of innovations in agriculture, industrial development and other sectors to address emerging challenges.
He also stressed that science popularisation in the mother tongue would help ensure that scientific knowledge and its benefits reach all sections of society.

Recalling his association with the University of Mysore and CSIR-CFTRI since his student days, he acknowledged Karnataka’s contributions to various fields and appreciated the Indian Botanical Society’s role in advancing botanical research and education.

The conference, being held from November 1 to 3, features 12 scientific sessions involving experts in botany and allied disciplines, besides eight thematic sections for oral presentations and poster presentations.

items.title: Trump’s midterm test: What India is watching as global power equations shift
points: America’s approaching midterm elections may test Donald Trump’s political strength, but for India, the stakes extend beyond who controls Capitol Hill.

In a conversation with Hindustan Times Senior Anchor Aayesha Varma on Point Blank, Executive Editor Shishir Gupta outlined a world in which electoral uncertainty intersects with diplomatic maneuvering and military pressure.
Gupta’s assessment of the November 3 US midterms was measured.

Asked about the implications for India, Gupta identified three principal concerns: a bilateral trade agreement, the inward-looking impulses of Trump’s Make America Great Again agenda, and Washington’s relationship with Pakistan.
Gupta pointed to H-1B visas and student admissions as areas where Washington’s domestic priorities could clash with Indian interests.
Gupta described closer US-Pakistan relations and Islamabad’s interest in upgrading American-origin equipment, including F-16 fighters, as developments New Delhi was watching closely.
Beyond bilateral concerns, Gupta identified Washington’s relationships with Moscow and Beijing as important variables for India.
Discussing the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting referred to in the conversation, he highlighted Ukraine and Iran as the central issues.

items.title: 61 illegal immigrants, mostly Bangladeshis, detained in Ahmedabad ahead of Diwali: Police
points: Legal procedures for the deportation of the detained persons were underway, the Crime Branch said in a press note.
The drive was conducted through intelligence gathering and coordinated raids across multiple zones of the city to identify foreign nationals residing in India illegally, it said.
The operation, which resulted in the detention of 61 illegal immigrants, was aimed at strengthening public safety and security ahead of the festive season, the police said.
Verification drives and legal action against illegal immigrants would continue, they said.
Last year, the Ahmedabad police detained more than 200 Bangladeshi nationals allegedly living illegally in different parts of the city.

In April 2025, following the Pahalgam terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir, the city police raided the Chandola Lake area and detained over 200 Bangladeshi nationals residing there illegally with the help of a local strongman, officials earlier said.

items.title: Indian R&D laggards underperform market as innovation-focused firms pull ahead
points: Within India’s listed corporate sector, average R&D expenditure as a share of sales actually declined from 0.64% in FY16 to 0.56% in FY26, even as absolute spending rose.

Indian listed companies that consistently grew their research and development spending have significantly outperformed the broader stock market over the past five years, according to an analysis published Monday by Monarch AIF.

The 130 companies that expanded R&D expenditure at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of over 20 per cent between FY21 and FY26 delivered an average stock-price CAGR of 23.5 per cent from April 2021 to September 2026 — nearly 10 percentage points above…
A smaller subset of 27 companies that also maintained R&D spending above 2 per cent of sales over three years posted an average CAGR of 32.5 per cent, more than double the benchmark index.
Only 28 of more than 2,000 listed Indian companies spend more than 5 per cent of sales on R&D, and just 59 exceed the 3 per cent mark.

items.title: Multibagger Engineers India shares jump 15% to 2-week high after Q2 results; stock gains 44% in 2026
points: Shares of Engineers India Ltd (EIL), a state-owned company, closed Monday’s trading session with a sharp 15% surge to settle at a two-week high of ₹290 apiece, as investors cheered the company’s upbeat September-quarter performance.
The rally also lifted the stock’s gains in 2026 to 44%.
For the September quarter, the company reported a net profit of ₹180 crore, a 66% increase over the previous quarter, supported by improved operating performance and strong business momentum.
In the first quarter, the company had reported a net profit of ₹108.5 crore.
In terms of operating performance, EBITDA, including other income, increased to ₹240 crore from ₹155 crore in the preceding quarter, while the EBITDA margin improved to 27% from 19%.
The company secured major orders worth ₹7,428 crore during the first half of FY27, comprising ₹5,762 crore from consultancy services and ₹1,666 crore from turnkey projects.
This took its total order book to a record ₹20,421 crore as of September 30.

items.title: El Niño likely to pose supply risks in mining and metals sector
points: ‘Operational and policy responses are already visible: Antofagasta (in Chile) cut guidance after severe weather in Chile, Peru has declared preventive flood emergencies for the 2026-27 event, and Zambia continues to ration power following the 2023-24…

Australia’s Office of Chief Economist (AOCE) said the intensification of the El Niño climate has implications for the demand and supply of energy commodities for heating and cooling, especially thermal coal.
On October 21, the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) said El Niño is likely to reach “unprecedented” risks, raising global weather risks.

Mines, smelters as well as port and transport infrastructure are likely to be affected, with the weather-related disruptions potentially constraining output and fuelling volatility across the broader complex, compounding supply chain pressures already seen…
Green Stocks Research said Chile, Peru and Zambia together mine close to 40 per cent of the world’s copper.
On the London Metal Exchange, the three-month copper contract ended at $14,154.50 a tonne over the weekend.

items.title: India tax filers shift toward investments and trading, says ClearTax data
points: The data signals a broad structural shift in how Indians earn and report income.
Nearly half, 47 per cent, of self-filers reported income from investments, business, freelancing, or cryptocurrency in AY 2026-27, compared to just 9.5 per cent in AY 2022-23.
The share of filers combining two or more such non-salary income sources rose from 3.5 per cent to 24.4 per cent over the same four-year period.
The proportion of filers reporting capital gains reached 41.7 per cent in AY 2026-27, up 7.3 percentage points from 34.4 per cent the year before.

ITR-3 filings, used by traders reporting business income from markets, surged from 20.6 per cent to 28.4 per cent of all filings in a single year, more than doubling its share from 13.5 per cent two years ago.
ITR-3 became the most commonly filed return in this age group, rising from 28 per cent to 44 per cent, while basic salary returns (ITR-1) fell from 41 per cent to 25 per cent.

items.title: Kuvempu University writes to Secretary of Higher Education for action on former Registrar (Evaluation)
points: the officer did not submit no-due certificates later, after furnishing necessary documents showing the expenses. | Photo Credit: FILE PHOTO Kuvempu University has written to the State government for action against its former Registrar (Evaluation), S.M.
Gopinath, over alleged irregularities in organising the 34th annual convocation held in January 2025.
Gopinath of Biotechnology at Davangere University, was posted as Registrar (Evaluation) at the Kuvempu University on August 22, 2023 and held the post until September 11, 2025.
Gopinath drew an advance ₹40 lakh as the Abstract Contingency Bill, a provision to obtain funds quickly for operational purposes.
Based on a report from the current Registrar (Evaluation), the university’s Finance Department carried out a preliminary audit.
The Finance Officer noted that the 32nd and 33rd convocations together cost about ₹33 lakh, whereas the expenditure on the 34th convocation exceeded ₹51.81 lakh.
Thimmarayappa, the current Registrar (Evaluation), said the 35th convocation was held during his tenure at a cost of about ₹20 lakh, and that he had already submitted the no-due certificates.

items.title: Delhi HC refuses to stay BS-VI curbs on outstation vehicles, hearing on Nov 27
points: The Delhi High Court on Monday refused to immediately stay the Delhi government’s notification barring vehicles registered outside the Capital that do not meet Bharat Stage-VI (BS-VI) emission standards from entering the city.

A bench of acting chief justice Nitin Sambre and justice Sanjay Sharma said a petition challenging the restrictions, filed by Faridabad-based lawyer Gurumukh Das Kohli, would be heard on November 27 along with a similar petition.
The restrictions came into force on Sunday as part of the Delhi government’s Winter Action Plan, which will remain in effect until January 31, 2027.

In his petition, Kohli said he owned a BS-IV petrol vehicle registered in Haryana and argued that the restriction discriminated between vehicles based on their place of registration rather than their actual emissions.

He contended that the blanket three-month restriction applied irrespective of daily air quality levels and was inconsistent with the Commission for Air Quality Management’s (CAQM) revised Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), which provides for restrictions…

items.title: Stena Launches Second Irish Sea Hybrid Ferry With Two 28m Rotor Sails That Cut Fuel Consumption By Up To 9%
points: Stena Line’s newest ship, Stena Connecta, was officially christened on October 16 at the CMI shipyard in Weihai, China.
The ship will soon embark on a voyage to its home port on the Irish Sea.
Together with Stena Futura, which entered service in September, these two new cargo ships increase cargo capacity on the Belfast–Heysham route by 40 percent.
The ceremony was attended by Stena Line CEO Niclas Mårtensson, members of the Stena Line management team, and Stena AB owner Dan Sten Olsson.
“Today we proudly celebrate another milestone for our fleet and our company.
Hybrid technology Stena Connecta is one of the new Max RoRo-ships built for maximum cargo capacity, with 2,800 avenue meters spread over a length of 147 meters.
The ship has a multi-hybrid propulsion system that allows the use of battery power, biofuel, and methanol.
In addition, it is equipped with two Norsepower Rotor sails (28 x 4 meters), which save up to 9 percent fuel on the route between Belfast and Heysham.

items.title: Amazon Great Indian Festival Diwali Edition Sale: Best Deals on Samsung Smartphones, iPhones
points: The festive season is in full swing right now.
But if you’re looking to upgrade your smartphone, then the market has seen phone prices rapidly climb due to an ongoing shortage of essential memory components.
This crunch has made already premium smartphones, particularly high-end flagships from brands like Samsung and Apple, even more expensive to purchase under normal circumstances.
Thankfully, the Amazon Great Indian Festival Diwali Edition sale has arrived just in time.
It offers a small window for buyers to grab these devices at significantly lower prices than their standard market rates ahead of Diwali.

items.title: GRAP-II pollution curbs imposed in Delhi-NCR as air quality dips further
points: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) on Monday invoked Stage II of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) across the National Capital Region (NCR) with immediate effect as Delhi's air quality deteriorated to the 'very poor' category for the…
The decision came as Delhi's Air Quality Index (AQI) climbed to 324 at 4pm on November 2.

In an order issued on Monday, the GRAP sub-committee said it reviewed the air quality situation along with forecasts from the India Meteorological Department (IMD) and the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM).
Pollution-related violations can be reported through the 311, Green Delhi and SAMEER apps.
It stood at 60 on Friday, following heavy rain that washed away pollutants and gave the Capital its cleanest October day in four years.
The reading increased to 117 in the 'moderate' category on October 31 and 261 in the 'poor' category on November 1, before reaching 324 on Monday.
Of Delhi's 59 air quality monitoring stations, data was available for 58 on Monday.

RIL's best day since 2020, Sebi’s LTCG rollback proposal lift Dalal Street
points: A rally in Reliance Industries (RIL) shares and growing optimism over a possible rollback of long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax for foreign investors gave Dalal Street plenty to cheer about on Monday, lifting both benchmark indices nearly 2%.
Buying picked up through the session, with RIL stock seeing its biggest intraday upmove since April 2020.
Sebi has recommended scrapping LTCG tax for foreign investors as India seeks to revive its underperforming equity markets, Reuters reported on Monday.
Sebi’s proposal is a step in the right direction, but tax efficiency alone will not bring foreign capital back to India, said Nirav Karkera, head of research and fund manager at W by Groww.
On Monday, Nifty 50 closed 1.68% higher at 23,440.80 and Sensex ended 1.66% up at 75,692.78.
RIL, which carries a 7.3% weight in the Nifty 50, surged 11.6% on NSE, its biggest single-day gain since it jumped 11.9% on 7 April 2020, according to Bloomberg data.

items.title: Rates crash: Gold price slips 7%, silver tanks 20% in Oct: Is Dhanteras 2026 right time to buy? What should investors do
points: Gold and silver prices have taken a sharp knock in October, offering some relief to buyers ahead of Dhanteras and Diwali 2026.
On the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), gold futures fell around 7% during the month, while silver futures plunged nearly 20% — almost three times gold's decline.
The correction has brought prices well below their January 2026 record highs, raising a familiar festive-season question: Is this the right time to buy precious metals, or could prices fall further?
MCX gold and silver futures rebounded on Monday, 2 November, recovering from the sharp sell-off towards the end of October as global bullion markets stabilised ahead of Dhanteras and Diwali.
The US Federal Reserve held rates in the 3.75%-4% range in October, but two members voted for a rate hike, while markets have begun pricing in the possibility of another increase in December.
MCX gold declined around 7% in October, while silver dropped nearly 20%.

items.title: An experience of rural life for urban students under government’s ‘Gramanubhava’
points: Students participating in Gramanubhava, an initiative aimed at familiarising the urban children with rural life, in Mysuru on November 1, 2026. | Photo Credit: M.A.

Sriram In an initiative aimed at familiarising the urban children with rural life, the Department of School Education has come out with a first-of-its-kind initiative called ‘Gramanubhava’ (Experiencing Rural Life).

Of 160 schools and PU colleges identified in the city limits of the State including 16 high schools and PU colleges within Mysuru urban limits have been selected for the implementation of this programme.

A total of 3,466 students studying in Class 9 and Class 11 from Mysuru have been identified to take part in this one day rural exposure visit which was formally flagged off by District Minister in-charge Yathindra Sidharamaiah on Sunday during the…
After the inauguration, 250 students travelled in five KSRTC buses to Bilikeri Hobli, Karimuddenahalli, Hanumanthapura, Yachanahalli and adjacent villages in Hunsur and T.

items.title: Autorickshaw driving empowers Mysuru women to become sole bread winners
points: Guru before an autorickshaw rally in Mysuru on Sunday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Once considered an unlikely livelihood for women, driving an autorickshaw has become powerful path of self-reliance for many women in Mysuru, who are the sole bread…

A total of 45 women drivers in the city have painstakingly rebuilt their lives, brick by brick, after losing the support of a male member (in most cases the husbands) of their family due to various reasons.
However, she found a new lease of life behind the wheel of an autorickshaw, earning an average of ₹1,000 a day.
During special occasions such as Dasara, her daily earnings go up to ₹1,500–2,000.

Chitra A.R., founder of the Taliru Foundation, who was present on the Ideal Java premises during an autorickshaw rally organised by women drivers to mark Karnataka Rajyotsava on Sunday, said, “Biggest challenge is accessing loans.

items.title: IndiGo moves beyond Stretch seats with lie-flat Business Class plans
points: IndiGo is going all-in on flat-bed business-class seats for its Airbus A350 widebodies, due to enter service in the second quarter of 2028, as well as for its future A321XLRs, according to its CEO William Walsh.
“The first A350 is due to be delivered in the second quarter of 2028.
It will come with 16 flat beds in the business class cabin.
The airline has locked down the configuration for the first 10 A350s out of a total of 60 on order, but the number of lie-flat business class seats could go up in the future.

The widebody Boeing 787s used on European routes, including Manchester, Amsterdam, Copenhagen, and London, were wet-leased from Norse and arrived with a preconfigured cabin that did not include Stretch seats.
That’s what the customer expects today.” IndiGo has taken the delivery of 4 A321 XLRs so far, and will add three more next year.
IndiGo has an order book of 40 XLRs, and took the delivery of its first XLR in January 2026.

items.title: HomeView to Double as Apple’s HomeKit Security Camera, Receive Dedicated Claude and ChatGPT Apps Soon, Tipster Claims
points: Apple is planning to bring multiple upgrades to the HomeView with the HomeView software 27.2 update.
In a post on X, user pdfu (@itspdfu) has shared that Apple’s HomeView will soon be able to act as a home security camera as part of the HomeKit environment.
The user spotted the functionality in the HomeView Software 27.2 update.

The update reportedly offers a better view of the “functionality and privacy protections.” The HomeView is said to work as a security camera with HomeKit Secure Video, and will be capable of activity detection, streaming, and recording.

items.title: Samsung Galaxy S27 Pro, Galaxy S27 Ultra Tipped to Feature Upgraded Privacy Display Technology
points: Privacy Display feature debuted with the Galaxy S26 Ultra.
This feature is designed to safeguard users' confidential details by hiding their full screen from others.
A new report states that the Galaxy S27 Pro and Galaxy S27 Ultra will feature an upgraded Privacy Display feature.
If the information proves accurate, the Galaxy S27 Pro would become the first non-Ultra Galaxy S flagship to feature Samsung's Privacy Display technology.

items.title: 'Don't need Dia Mirza to teach us how to celebrate': Mumbai mayor on BMC's pollution-free Diwali video takedown
points: Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde on Monday defended the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC)'s decision to take down a video featuring actor Dia Mirza on celebrating pollution-free Diwali.
Hitting out at the actor, Tawde said Hindus are well aware of how to celebrate Diwali and don't need Mirza to “teach them”.
“Regarding how Hindus should celebrate Diwali—we certainly do not need Dia Mirza to teach us.
Even as Tawde slammed the actor, deputy mayor Sanjay Ghadi defended Mirza's appeal against bursting firecrackers.
According to news agency PTI, Mirza's video was removed within hours of Satam's comment, even as campaign videos featuring actors Madhuri Dixit, Nishigandha Wad and others were retained.
The BMC's post accompanying Mirza's video stated that in accordance with the Bombay High Court's directives, bursting firecrackers on public roads, lanes and footpaths was strictly prohibited.
Backing the BMC's decision to remove Mirza's clip, Mumbai mayor Ritu Tawde said she has always “sided with divisive forces”, news agency PTI quoted her as saying.

items.title: Indian Navy Orders 8 Next Generation Corvettes In Rs 53,866 Crore Deal
points: The Ministry of Defence has signed contracts worth Rs 53,866.50 crore with Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Limited (GRSE) and Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL) for the acquisition of eight Next Generation Corvettes (NGCs) for the Indian Navy.
The contracts were inked in the presence of Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh at Kartavya Bhawan-2, New Delhi, on November 02, 2026.
Under the contracts, GRSE will construct five corvettes, while GSL will construct the remaining three.

The project marks a significant milestone in India’s indigenous warship design and construction capabilities, as it is the first project in which the ships will be indigenously designed by the Indian Navy and constructed by Defence Public Sector…

The NGCs will be equipped with state-of-the-art capabilities, including advanced missiles, weapons and sensor suites, enabling them to undertake missions across the air, surface and sub-surface domains.

The NGC project will provide a significant impetus to India’s indigenous shipbuilding ecosystem by strengthening collaboration among DPSUs, private shipyards and Indian industrial partners, including MSMEs.

items.title: ChatGPT Health Could Soon Get Google Health Integration on Android: Report
points: OpenAI may be exploring deeper health data integration for ChatGPT on Android through Google's Health Connect platform.
References found in the app's code point to permissions covering physical measurements, reproductive health information and background access to health records.
The findings also suggest that ChatGPT could introduce additional interfaces to explain its data access requirements.
The potential integration would bring Android users closer to the health data sharing experience that iPhone users already have through Apple Health, although OpenAI has not confirmed the feature.

The police executed synchronized raids across different localities to pinpoint foreign nationals living without legal status.
Deportation processes are currently being initiated, furthering previous measures aimed at curbing illegal immigration from Bangladesh.
